relevance_note: The paper describes three patients with heterozygous TNFAIP3 missense variants ("three patients with missense variants (Glu192Lys, Ile310Thr, and Gln709Arg)") plus three carrier relatives.
method_note: Read the full paper and wrote every row by hand into a Python builder script (no automated table transcription). Table 1 has patients as columns (header row '| | P1 | P2 | P3 |'; P1/P2/P3 = Patient 1/2/3 of the text); Table 2 has variants as columns (header '| | p.Glu192Lys | p.Ile310Thr | p.Gln709Arg |'); spans quote each row from its label through the relevant cell. Relatives are labelled with the paper's own words: 'His father' (father of Patient 1), 'Her mother' (mother of Patient 2), 'Her father' (father of Patient 3). The other parents were sequenced ('Sanger sequencing was performed for the patients and their parents'; WES on patient 3 and her parents) but no result is stated, so they get no rows. Variants used only as functional-assay controls (Phe127Cys, Lys417Serfs*4, Cys243Tyr, Met476Ile, Thr647Pro, Gln709His, Gln709del) belong to no individual here and are not recorded. Patient 2's two MEFV variants are attributed to her unambiguously and are recorded. Inheritance is 'not reported' for every variant: the paper says each relative 'had the same variant' but never states inheritance; relatives' zygosity is also left 'not reported'. is_proband = true for Patients 1-3 is a judgement (they are the ascertained patients whose relatives are described relative to them); the paper never uses 'proband' or 'index case'. Contradiction (Patient 2): 'a high level of serum CRP' with the fever/abdominal-pain episodes versus 'Serum inflammatory reactants were negative during the intermittent episodes of fever' (possibly meaning between episodes); both feature rows emitted and the checklist item 'elevated inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR)' set to 'not reported'. Contradiction (Ile310Thr frequency): text gives 'The prevalence of the Ile310Thr allele was 0.0002 in Europe' but Table 2 gives 'Frequency in Europe^a | NA | 0.00002'; not extracted into any field. Patient 3's 'Age of onset' is 12 y in Table 1 although cerebral palsy (postnatal day 1) and epilepsy (age 4 years) came earlier; recorded as printed. Age at diagnosis for Patient 3 is the SLE diagnosis at 24 years; no age at genetic diagnosis is given for anyone. Patient 1's repeated tonsillitis, lymphadenitis and bronchitis are not called infections (and 'no significant pathogens were detected' during fevers), so 'recurrent infections' is 'not reported'. 'Recurrent stomatitis' in Patient 1's father is not stated to be ulcerative, so 'oral ulcers' is 'not reported' for him. Asymptomatic relatives ('lacked any symptoms') get one excluded feature row; the global statement was not expanded into excluded checklist items. Patient 3 had a single 'fever' at 24 years, so 'recurrent fever' is 'not reported'; a positive direct Coombs test without stated cytopenia leaves 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' 'not reported'. The group statement that DNT, Treg, Th17 and Tfh cells 'tended to increase' in the present patients was not extracted (no individual values).
